facts.topic: 6. register.py
facts.fact: What it does (study copy, 30 lines, identical in both run folders): reads the settings from the environment through configuration.resolve_settings (ARCI_QUICKSTART_BASELINE, ARCI_QUICKSTART_CANDIDATE, ARCI_QUICKSTART_TEMPERATURE, default 0.7 for real models; reasoning False for ollama: ids); writes them as `quickstart_settings` into every line of tasks.jsonl; sets rule.scenario_seeds to 'per_round' for real models ('fixed' for offline:scripted); rewrites arci.yaml with yaml.safe_dump(sort_keys=False), which drops comments and changes layout, so file digests must be taken after it. It makes no model call. It prints 'Registered model settings; start a new run with arci run arci.yaml'.

facts.topic: 6. register.py
facts.fact: When it must be run: with the three variables exported, before the digests are computed and the pre-registration is committed, and again whenever a model id or the temperature changes. The same variables must be exported for `arci run`: agent.py's registered_tools calls validate_registration(task) for each trial and raises 'quickstart environment disagrees with registered settings; run python register.py before starting a new experiment' when the environment differs from what tasks.jsonl holds (a set-up failure is an ERROR, not a FAIL, per decision D-08).

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: what is compared
facts.fact: The suite gate compares one number: Delta = the unweighted mean, over the N registered (task, condition) cells, of E[Y_B - Y_A], where Y is the binary PASS/FAIL of candidate B and baseline A. A round runs every cell once with one baseline and one candidate trial; each pair gives d in {-1, 0, +1}. A verdict concerns this mean and can hide a regression in one cell; per-cell counts are descriptive and give no verdict. The grid and its weights may not be chosen after seeing results.

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: rule, alpha, delta, stakes
facts.fact: Defaults alpha 1/20, delta 1/10, stakes {1/4, 1/2}, max_rounds ceil(400/N). For each stake q: lambda=q/(1-delta), mu=q/(1+delta); PASS wealth is the average over stakes of prod[1+lambda(d+delta)], BLOCK wealth the average of prod[1-mu(d+delta)]; a test crosses when its wealth >= 2/alpha (40 at defaults), inclusive, in exact arithmetic. Stakes are fixed bet sizes in an equal-weight mixture, 1 to 8 strictly increasing values in (0,1), not selectable from outcomes. alpha is the total error budget, split alpha/2 per direction; delta is the non-inferiority margin on the suite-mean success difference (1/10 = 10 points). Allowed: alpha in [1/1000000, 1/2], delta in (0,1).

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: what PASS, BLOCK, INCONCLUSIVE assert and the error bounds
facts.fact: PASS rejects H0: Delta <= -delta (asserts non-inferiority within delta, nothing about absolute reliability); P(ever PASS-crossed | Delta <= -delta) <= alpha/2. Statistical BLOCK rejects H0: Delta >= -delta ("establishes a drop exceeding delta"); P(ever BLOCK-crossed | Delta >= -delta) <= alpha/2. At Delta = -delta the union is <= alpha. There is no extra alpha charge per registered round. INCONCLUSIVE establishes neither. At defaults each directional error is at most 2.5%. These are repeated-experiment probabilities, not posteriors. Priority at each complete round end: errored pairs over tolerance -> ERROR; candidate hard violation -> BLOCK; both crossed -> ERROR; PASS crossed -> PASS; BLOCK crossed -> BLOCK; else INCONCLUSIVE, and stop INCONCLUSIVE at max_rounds without changing the boundary.

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: assumptions behind the bound
facts.fact: The bound assumes joint independence across cells within a round and across rounds, the same per-cell law in every round, every cell exactly once per look, and no execution-order effect (arm order is hashed per round and can flip). Within-pair dependence is unrestricted. With scenario_seeds per_round (what register.py selects for real models and what runs 1 and 2 used) the guarantee additionally requires that in every round the suite mean over that round's scenario instances obeys the null; ARCI does not check this and gives no guarantee averaged over seeds. The run 2 log prints this sentence. Common-mode failures (for example a model server incident in one arm) are outside the bound.

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: rounds
facts.fact: Looks happen only at the end of complete balanced rounds; a partial round is not a look. The runner stops at the first non-INCONCLUSIVE round or at the registered cap. No other look, trial retry, rescheduling after error, extension of the cap, or resume is supported. A new run is a new campaign; listing prior runs does not reset the error budget, and retrying an unchanged candidate until PASS is outside the guarantee.

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: if the candidate is truly better
facts.fact: There is no superiority verdict. A truly better candidate can only get PASS (reason text "non-inferiority established"), which asserts Delta > -delta and nothing more. The earliest possible PASS when every pair favours the candidate is 9 pairs, decided at the next complete round end. arci plan confirms: with baseline 0.72 and candidate 0.95 (independent arms) PASS has probability 0.999999 or more after about one round at 24, 40, 96 and 120 cells. So with the fix as candidate, the expected result PASS would not show that the fix helps.

facts.topic: 1 Verdict: swapping the arms to show X better than Y by more than the margin
facts.fact: The proof names the arms only A and B and uses nothing about which is new, so with baseline = set-up X (with the fix) and candidate = set-up Y (without), a statistical BLOCK asserts mean(Y_Y - Y_X) < -delta, that is X's suite-mean pass rate exceeds Y's by more than delta, with false-claim probability at most alpha/2 under the same assumptions. In that orientation PASS asserts X's gain is below delta. This is my reading of the stated guarantee: the documentation describes only the regression question and does not mention or forbid the swapped use. Role-dependent parts to state in a pre-registration: (a) a candidate hard violation forces BLOCK outside the statistical bound, but hard violations arise only from max_tool_calls, forbidden_tools, required_tools and max_calls_per_tool, and the run 2 manifest's contract declares only the oracle; (b) the reason text reads "regression established" and reports say baseline/candidate; (c) earlier runs are matched by suite_id and candidate_id; (d) a warning prints if the baseline passes fewer than half its trials.

facts.topic: 3 Faults: names and what each delivers
facts.fact: Registered names: tool_timeout, tool_error_once, empty_result, decision_low_confidence, decision_unavailable. Suites refuse the two decision faults and the ceiling bucket. tool_timeout and tool_error_once act before the tool: the real tool is not executed and the call returns ok=False with error_kind "timeout" or "error", detail "injected timeout"/"injected error", injected_by set. empty_result acts after the tool: the real tool runs, then its value is replaced by None with ok still True and injected_by "empty_result". Each fires only on the named tool (or any tool) at that tool's zero-based occurrence, default 0. In the LangChain adapter the timeout and error kinds become the exceptions given in fault_exceptions and the study's ToolRetryMiddleware retries them once; an empty result is ordinary JSON null, raises nothing, and is not retried by code.

facts.topic: 3 Faults: custom value or text
facts.fact: No built-in fault takes a replacement value: empty_result hard-codes None, and params is read only by decision_low_confidence. But a fault name may be a custom factory module:function; ARCI imports it in the trial process and scopes it to the declared tool and occurrence. Its after() may return the result with any JSON value (for example a text) and an injected_by name, and FaultSpec.params is a free dictionary. So a condition can deliver a text in place of a tool result without changing ARCI. A condition, however, applies to both arms of a cell (one condition and one seed per pair), and the verdict compares arms, never conditions, so a custom fault cannot be the difference between the arms.

facts.topic: 3 Faults: smallest per-arm way without changing ARCI
facts.fact: It has to be a middleware in the study's agent.py, added to one arm's settings; tools.py cannot do it. Reasons: there is one toolset factory for both arms with signature (task, seed) and no arm argument, and empty_result is applied at the boundary after the tool function has returned, so code inside tools.py never sees the null. User middleware sits between the adapter's outer and inner middleware (create_agent(middleware=[outer, *middleware, inner])), so its wrap_tool_call receives the result after the boundary. Reader B's variant would replace the null content of a lookup_order result with a text; Reader A's variant would call handler(request) once more, the same mechanism ToolRetryMiddleware uses, and each such attempt passes through the boundary, is recorded, and counts against max_tool_calls. Middleware is trusted code in this adapter. I did not execute either middleware (no trial was run).

The store does not record what the model was shown: model_step events carry only {"summary": "model"}. So a replacement text (Reader B) would not appear in the store, only in agent.py; a code retry (Reader A) would appear as a second lookup_order start/finish at occurrence 1 with no model_step between the two. A custom fault's name in fault accounting is resolved by importing the factory in a 2-second subprocess, otherwise the row reads "cannot attribute".

facts.topic: 4 Limiting the suite
facts.fact: A suite is always the full grid tasks x conditions; N = number of tasks times number of conditions. There is no per-task condition subset, and conditions are used as declared (no clean condition is added). Limiting means declaring fewer conditions (one is allowed) and/or fewer tasks in the task file: 24 tasks x empty_result = 24 cells; the 8 stock-note tasks x empty_result = 8 cells. Any such change alters the rule digest, so it is a new experiment id with new seeds.

facts.topic: 5 arci plan: what it computes
facts.fact: Two modes. Without a suite file it is the v1 planner (fixed-sample Clopper-Pearson, K=1, N <= 400 per arm, needs --target-verdict); that is not the suite rule. With a suite descriptor or sealed manifest as the positional argument it uses the registered rule (and refuses --alpha, --delta, --n-grid, --looks and the target options), prints the rule and three floors (earliest PASS round, earliest BLOCK round, never-differs PASS round), and, given a model, the exact probabilities of PASS, BLOCK and INCONCLUSIVE and the expected pairs. The model is either homogeneous (--baseline-rate, --candidate-rate and --agreement = P(both arms give the same outcome), all three required) or per-cell joint laws from --cell-laws JSON. Assumed: cells and rounds independent, the same law every round, no errors or hard violations; "model projections, not measured live-agent behavior". It refuses to enumerate above 8192 denominator bits or 1e11 estimated bit-operations and then prints floors only. The descriptor is compiled without importing the agent modules.

designs.what_each_verdict_means:
The rule tests Delta = mean over the 8 cells of E[pass(candidate) - pass(baseline)] = mean of (pass without the text - pass with the text).

BLOCK (the tool prints "regression established"): Delta < -1/10. On these 8 cells the set-up without the text passes less often than the set-up with it, by more than 10 points. Read: the sentence raised the pass rate by more than 10 points here. If the true gain is 10 points or less, the chance of ever getting this verdict is at most 2.5 percent.

PASS (the tool prints "non-inferiority established"): Delta > -1/10. The set-up without the text is not more than 10 points below the one with it; the sentence's gain here is below 10 points, and may be zero or negative. If the true gain is 10 points or more, the chance of this verdict is at most 2.5 percent.

INCONCLUSIVE: neither after 40 rounds. Published as such; the counts are then description only.

ERROR: more than 4 errored pairs. Published as ERROR.

Does the documented guarantee support this reading? Yes for the arithmetic, with one caveat to state openly. The proof (docs/STATISTICS_SUITE.md:10-37, 90-142) names the arms only A and B and uses nothing about which one is new, and nothing requires the arms to differ by model (the shipped quickstart compares two set-ups of one model). But the documentation describes only the regression question and neither mentions nor forbids the swapped use; the report will say baseline, candidate, "regression" and "non-inferiority", so the write-up must translate, and must say this is the maintainer's reading of the stated bound. Role-dependent parts: hard violations (none possible here), the warning printed when the baseline passes under half its trials (it may print if the text arm passes under half; it concerns absolute reliability only, src/arci/cli.py:507-511), and prior-run matching by suite id and candidate id. The bound assumes independence across cells and rounds and, with per_round seeds, that each round's own scenario instances obey the null; ARCI does not check that (docs/STATISTICS_SUITE.md:165-236). Neither verdict says the text closes "most of the gap", why the model behaves so, or anything outside these 8 cells.
